Everything below is executed by R when the page renders. The code is visible by
default; click **Code** to fold it, or use the code menu at the top right to
download the source.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

cars <- mtcars |>
  tibble::as_tibble(rownames = "model") |>
  mutate(
    cylinders   = factor(cyl, levels = c(4, 6, 8), labels = c("4-cyl", "6-cyl", "8-cyl")),
    transmission = factor(am, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("Automatic", "Manual"))
  )

glimpse(cars)
```

## Weight against fuel economy

Heavier cars drink more, and the relationship is close to linear within each
cylinder count.

```{r}
#| label: fig-weight-mpg
#| fig-cap: "Fuel economy falls with weight; the gap between 4- and 8-cylinder cars persists at any given weight."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.5

ggplot(cars, aes(wt * 1000, mpg, colour = cylinders)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.6, alpha = .85) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, linewidth = .7) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#2f6f4e", "#c08a2e", "#8c3b3b")) +
  labs(
    x = "Weight (lb)", y = "Miles per gallon", colour = NULL,
    title = "Fuel economy against weight",
    subtitle = "32 cars, Motor Trend 1974"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

@fig-weight-mpg is cross-referenced with `@fig-weight-mpg` — Quarto numbers the
figure and makes the reference a link.

## A quick model

```{r}
#| label: tbl-model
#| tbl-cap: "Least-squares fit of mpg on weight and cylinder count."

fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt + cylinders, data = cars)

broom::tidy(fit, conf.int = TRUE) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

Each extra 1000 lb costs roughly `r abs(round(coef(fit)[["wt"]], 1))` mpg, holding
cylinder count fixed. That number isn't typed in — it's an *inline* R expression,
written like this:

```markdown
Each extra 1000 lb costs roughly `{r} abs(round(coef(fit)[["wt"]], 1))` mpg.
```

(In a `.qmd` the inline form is a backtick span starting with `r`.) Refit the model
and the sentence updates itself, so the prose can never drift away from the numbers.

## Group summaries

```{r}
#| label: tbl-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Mean fuel economy by cylinder count and transmission."

cars |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_mpg = round(mean(mpg), 1),
    sd_mpg   = round(sd(mpg), 1),
    .by = c(cylinders, transmission)
  ) |>
  arrange(cylinders, transmission) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Cylinders", "Transmission", "n", "Mean mpg", "SD"))
```

Because `freeze: auto` is set in `posts/_metadata.yml`, this code runs once and the
results are cached in `_freeze/`. Later site builds reuse them until this file
changes — so rendering the site stays fast, and a post written today still builds
years from now even if the packages have moved on.
